svg.title: Escape Room Adventure | Unique items, automatic acquisition and room gates

g.text: Escape Room Adventure | Unique items, automatic acquisition and room gates
Every configured item exists exactly once: in one ROOM
or in INVENTORY. Each configured item has one original room.
Actions and first room entry automatically transfer the SAME
appearing items into inventory and set revealed=true.
Preflight all IDs before any effects, completion or transfers.
Already-held IDs are skipped; no second copy is constructed.
Items remain in inventory when used by actions or the door.
Getters expose read-only copies, never mutable containers.
Each room owns exactly two independent gates:
its door ItemLock and its exit TriviaLock.
Interactables complete their own actions and own no locks.
Item and answer operations stay in the relevant subtype.
No public unconditional unlock() bypasses validation.
Already-unlocked is a no-op before item or answer checks.
ItemLock requires a nonempty set of configured item IDs.
against the actual inventory; passing a list of IDs is insufficient.
One Room composes text-based objects, choices and gates.
nextRoomId is the one configured successor; empty means final.
isFinal() derives from nextRoomId.isEmpty(), without a stored flag.
The two gates may be completed in either order.
Neither gate's validation depends on the other gate's state.
allLocks includes exactly the door and exit Trivia;
availableActions excludes completed one-shot or inaccessible actions.
collectables contains only the remaining ROOM items.
findCollectable resolves those objects; visibleCollectables is internal.
takeCollectable may transfer a prevalidated previously hidden item.
Game.move() rechecks status and both gates, then preflights the
configured destination and its visible-item transfers before mutation.
A present nextRoomId calls enterRoom; empty sets ESCAPED.
Final completion cannot bypass either gate.
Escaped games reject mutations; no backward navigation is exposed.
interact resolves any selected item from the actual inventory.
Prepare/validate the exact object/action plan, then preflight ALL
appearingItemIds: skip held IDs; otherwise require the current room's
remaining item. Missing targets abort before any mutation.
Commit applyInteraction then acquireItems as one serial command.
acquireItems uses takeCollectable / reveal / Inventory.add and returns
only newly transferred objects; other held items remain unchanged.
Append "Obtained: labels" to resultText only for these new transfers.
Repeatable appearances skip held IDs but may apply other effects;
changed records actual object/completion/location changes only.
itemDetails resolves requested IDs across all rooms and inventory;
it returns read-only metadata without exposing snapshot answers.
useItems resolves only the current room's door ItemLock
and delegates tryUnlock(inventory); no selected item list is trusted.
Trivia operations resolve only the current room's exit TriviaLock.
Wrong IDs, missing items, wrong answers and failed conditions
leave state unchanged. Commands run on the serial worker.
New-game construction calls enterRoom(startingRoomId) before publication.
enterRoom preflights visibleCollectables, then commits room entry and
automatic acquisition. Future-room visible items stay ROOM until entry.
Start presents the brand-new inventory's obtained names once.
Final completion acquires no next-room items.
Restore uses a state constructor, never enterRoom or acquisition.
Rendering, getters, saving, loading and Trivia never grant or reannounce items.
Interactable owns its actions and completedActionIds.
Only nonrepeatable actions record completion; repeatable actions may run again.
An optional requiredItemId must identify an item actually held.
appearingItemIds is immutable, may be empty and names own-room items.
Repeated references identify the same unique configured items.
Conditions and effects access object state only; effects never unlock gates.
Room validates state-effect targets; Game preflights appearance locations.
Validate the full plan and all transfers before effects/completion commit.
Descriptions and resultText carry story information.
GameStatus = ACTIVE | ESCAPED; LockKind = ITEM | TRIVIA.
DomainResult is immutable: { code: ResultCode, changed: boolean,
ActionOption is immutable: { objectId, actionId, label, requiresItem }.
ResultCode distinguishes missing/wrong items, wrong answers,
completed actions, unmet conditions and unmet exit gates.
Stored relationships are explicit fields; lines describe those SAME fields.
Entity/item/lock IDs are globally unique; action IDs are unique per object.
Trivia compares trimmed answers case-insensitively; leading zeroes remain significant.
Constructors validate references, nonempty ItemLock item sets,
exactly one original room per item, object/action pairs and local appearance IDs.
Successors form one finite path from startingRoomId through EVERY room
exactly once, ending with nextRoomId empty. Reject broken references,
self-loops, cycles, branching and unreachable rooms.
Required items are obtainable in this room or earlier on the path,
before either current-room gate; later-room dependencies are invalid.
Initial/restored state is complete before an aggregate becomes usable.
Save schema 4 stores ROOM | INVENTORY item locations, objects/actions,
locks/questions, generated values and game position/status.
Successors come from the matching immutable template, not the snapshot.
Every room preceding the restored current room must have both gates passed.
Change templateVersion whenever successors or appearance rules change.
Schema 4 adds no acquisition ledger; restore preserves saved locations exactly.
Previous schemas and invalid snapshots are rejected before publication.
Trivia.expectedAnswer stays private and is omitted from UI output.
Entities never import Swing, JSON, HTTP or application output models.
Behavior and data-access diagrams expand this same domain contract.
